title: NuGet.Config
description: Configuring NuGet package sources, credentials, and restore behavior.

data.text: `NuGet.Config` is the XML file that tells NuGet where packages come from and how restore behaves. It lists package sources, credentials, and settings such as the global packages folder. NuGet merges several files at once — solution, user (`%APPDATA%\NuGet\NuGet.Config`), and machine — with the closest file taking precedence.

terms.definition: The feeds NuGet searches, each with a key and a v3 index URL.
Restricts which patterns are allowed to resolve from which source — useful to prevent dependency confusion.
Settings such as globalPackagesFolder, repositoryPath, and signatureValidationMode.

data.title: Example NuGet.Config
data.content: Define a public feed and a private feed, and map package patterns to sources so a typo cannot silently resolve from the wrong feed.
data.code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <packageSources>
    <clear />
    <add key="nuget.org" value="https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json" />
    <add key="MyPrivateFeed" value="https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/org/_packaging/feed/nuget/v3/index.json" />
  </packageSources>

  <packageSourceMapping>
    <packageSource key="nuget.org">
      <package pattern="*" />
    </packageSource>
    <packageSource key="MyPrivateFeed">
      <package pattern="Contoso.*" />
    </packageSource>
  </packageSourceMapping>
</configuration>

data.title: Manage sources from the CLI
data.content: The CLI edits the config for you instead of hand-editing XML.
data.code:
# List configured sources
dotnet nuget list source

# Add a private feed with a name
dotnet nuget add source https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/org/_packaging/feed/nuget/v3/index.json \
  --name MyPrivateFeed

# Remove a source
dotnet nuget remove source MyPrivateFeed

# Inspect where packages are cached and clear a cache
dotnet nuget locals all --list
dotnet nuget locals http-cache --clear

data.title: Keep credentials out of the repo
data.text: Prefer credential providers (`dotnet nuget add source --username ... --password ... --store-password-in-clear-text` is for local only) or environment-variable based authentication in CI. Never commit a `NuGet.Config` containing a plaintext API key — that file is read by every developer and build agent on the machine.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NuGet.Config controls sources, credentials, and restore settings
Multiple config files merge, closest wins; `<clear />` resets inherited sources
`dotnet nuget` manages sources and caches from the CLI
data.takeaway: A reviewed NuGet.Config makes restores deterministic and keeps private feeds private.
